detail: Will sweep DEPTH (and derived width via ASPECT_RATIO/HEAD_DIM) to find the compute-optimal model size for the fixed 5-min budget; will not assume the baseline DEPTH=8 is optimal for this time budget. Will not touch optimizer internals unless depth sweep plateaus.

detail: Explore model depth (n_layer) and aspect-ratio changes vs baseline DEPTH=8, retuning LR scale factors accordingly since the model exposes a dmodel_lr_scale already. title: model depth/width scaling
detail: Explore the depth vs width tradeoff (DEPTH, ASPECT_RATIO, HEAD_DIM) under the fixed 5-min time budget, since more layers costs more time/step but may give better bpb per token; I will not assume LR schedule or optimizer changes are the bottleneck.

title: model scale & batch size tuning
detail: Will sweep DEPTH (model width/depth via ASPECT_RATIO) and TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE/DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE to find compute-optimal size for the fixed 5-min budget. Will not assume the baseline DEPTH=8 is optimal for this short budget; will not touch optimizer internals (Muon/AdamW math) or attention mechanism.

title: optimizer/schedule hyperparameters

Will not assume the current linear warmdown or dmodel_lr_scale=1/sqrt is already optimal at fixed depth.

title: optimizer & schedule tuning
detail: Pivoting off depth/width (4 peers already claimed that family). Will tune LR magnitudes, WARMDOWN_RATIO, WEIGHT_DECAY schedule, and Muon momentum schedule at fixed baseline DEPTH=8 architecture. Will not touch model architecture/shape.

text: Stacking my WEIGHT_DECAY=0.1 finding with a1's WARMDOWN_RATIO=0.7 finding (both independent wins on the batch2^18+softcap10 base): val_bpb 0.986379, NEW BEST for the cell, marginally better than either alone (WD=0.1 alone: 0.986436; WARMDOWN=0.7 alone: 0.986867). The two changes compose but the gain from stacking is small (~0.0001 vs WD alone) — mostly WD=0.1 was already capturing the benefit. My share (6/6) is now spent.

DEPTH=10 (deeper/narrower, model_dim scales via ASPECT_RATIO=64) on top of the batch2^18+softcap=10 base: val_bpb 0.985651, a NEW BEST, clearly better than DEPTH=8 on the same base (0.987594-0.987994, n=3 independent runs). This contradicts the earlier consensus that 'baseline DEPTH=8 is well-tuned' — that conclusion was reached under the OLD (larger) batch size. Under the smaller-batch/more-steps regime, going deeper (not shallower) pays off: DEPTH=6 clearly hurts (1.035902, see disconfirmation #302) but DEPTH=10 helps. VRAM headroom was fine (peak 67.8GB). Suggests the depth/width optimum shifted when batch size was halved; worth retesting DEPTH=12 in this regime.
